claims.text: Men who consumed alcohol three to four days per week had a decreased risk of myocardial infarction compared with men who consumed alcohol less than once per week.
Men who consumed alcohol five to seven days per week had a decreased risk of myocardial infarction compared with men who consumed alcohol less than once per week.
The decreased risk of myocardial infarction was similar between men consuming less than 10 g of alcohol per drinking day and those consuming 30 g or more.
No single type of alcoholic beverage conferred an additional risk reduction for myocardial infarction beyond drinking frequency.
Consumption of alcohol with meals did not substantially alter the inverse association with myocardial infarction risk.
A 12.5-g increase in daily alcohol consumption over a four-year follow-up period was associated with a decreased risk of myocardial infarction.

evidence.description: Multivariate relative risk of 0.68 (95% CI, 0.55 to 0.84) for men consuming alcohol 3 to 4 days per week vs. less than once per week.
Multivariate relative risk of 0.63 (95% CI, 0.54 to 0.74) for men consuming alcohol 5 to 7 days per week vs. less than once per week.
Risk of myocardial infarction was similar among men who consumed less than 10 g of alcohol per drinking day and those who consumed 30 g or more.
No single type of beverage conferred additional benefit among beer, red wine, white wine, and liquor.
Consumption with meals did not confer additional benefit or substantially alter the inverse association.
A 12.5-g increase in daily alcohol consumption over a four-year period was associated with a relative risk of myocardial infarction of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.62 to 0.99).

methodologies.name: Prospective cohort study using repeated food-frequency questionnaires
methodologies.description: Prospective evaluation of 38,077 male health professionals assessing individual beverage intake every four years to track nonfatal myocardial infarction and fatal coronary heart disease events over 12 years.
conditions: Free of cardiovascular disease and cancer at baseline

limitations.text: The roles of drinking pattern and type of alcoholic beverage in coronary heart disease risk reduction remain unclear in prior research.
